catalyst.action: AMENDS the pending 134.50 entry published 2026-08-21, which was a breakout level above the 120-day high of 134.125 and could never have filled. thesis: Dollar General reported Q2 FY2026 on 2026-08-27 with net sales up 5.2% to 11.3B, same-store sales up 3.5%, operating profit up 29.2% to 769.2M and diluted EPS up 33.3% to 2.48, and raised FY2026 EPS guidance to 7.80-8.00 from 7.20-7.45. The number that matters for a multi-year thesis is the composition of the comp: customer traffic up 2.0% against ticket up 1.5%, which is market share rather than pricing. That is the trade-down mechanism working in real time, and the macro I found today - a 10-year at 5.275%, the highest since 2002, with consumer durables being destroyed around it at WHR -49.1% and LCII -40.5% - is the condition under which it keeps working. Stripping the roughly 0.25 of non-recurring tariff-refund benefit from guidance leaves about 7.65 of clean FY2026 EPS, putting the stock at 16.1x today and the 110.00 accumulation level at 14.4x.
key_risk: INVALIDATION CONDITION, since this carries no stop: same-store sales turning negative for two consecutive quarters, or customer traffic turning negative in any quarter while comps stay positive on ticket alone. The second is the subtle one - comps held up by price with traffic falling would mean the share gain has stopped and the company is simply passing through inflation, which is the opposite of this thesis. Separately, the Street does not agree: analyst bullish share is only 45.0% with 21 holds and slightly deteriorating, so a re-rating requires the holds to move.
counter_argument: The strongest case against is that dollar stores are structurally low-margin retailers with a history of margin give-back, that a 33% EPS gain flattered by tariff refunds is not a run rate, and that at 16.1x the stock is not actually cheap for what it is - which is why the recommendation is to wait rather than to buy. The answer to the valuation half is that the bear case here is not a guess: the stock traded at 99.57 within the last 120 days, which is 13.0x clean guided EPS, so 13x is a multiple this market has already paid. Anchoring the downside at a price actually printed this quarter, rather than at a modelled one, is what makes the 2.66 reward-to-risk at a 110.00 entry real - and the same arithmetic at 123.27 gives 0.63, which is why today is not the day.
